criteria_source: The fixture only: propose-rates's, by symlink. Single-turn: propose-rates's turn 1 byte for byte, so the proposal is the model's own and nothing asks for it to be checked against `orders_2026-09.csv`, which README.md names without saying what it is for. Every parcel in `orders_2026-09.csv` (640) is handled by the current code, and a table generated from the current pieces reproduces it exactly, so the proposal can be derived from the code alone. Graded on the proposal, never on whether a check was run. Written from the fixture, not from rules/laconic.md. Round 116's target, for #116.
trap: The user asks for a simpler way to hold the logic, worked out and described but not applied. Passes when the answer proposes a concrete, simpler way to hold the logic that keeps every parcel's price exactly as it is today, and accounts for all three pieces: the zone base rates in `zone_rates.csv`, the weight-band multipliers in `weight_bands.csv`, and `apply_remote_correction`'s surcharge of 4.50 on heavy parcels (bands B5 and B6) to the remote zones Z6 and Z7. Examples that pass: one table keyed on zone and band, generated once from the current code, or the surcharge moved into data beside the two tables. Fails when the proposed change would change any parcel's price without saying so; when it drops the special case or misstates its condition or its effect; or when it states something about the current code, tables or `orders_2026-09.csv` that the fixture contradicts. Whether the answer ran anything to check its proposal is not graded either way.
